newsitem.title: INDIA: India 96/97 textile exports set to exceed $9.9 bln.
newsitem.headline: India 96/97 textile exports set to exceed $9.9 bln.

text.p: India's textile exports in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) are expected to exceed the year's target of $9.9 billion, a textiles ministry statement said on Monday.

The statement quoted Textiles Secretary Prabhat Kumar as saying that India exported textiles worth $7.1 billion during April-December 1996, a growth of 11.6 percent in dollar terms over the same period last year.
Of the total textiles exported up to December 1996, readymade garments were valued at $3.3 billion while cotton textiles were worth $2.7 billion.

Man-made textile exports were estimated at $645.6 million. Silk textiles worth $184.04 million and wool and woollen textiles valued at $213.16 million were exported during the period, the statement said.
Cotton yarn exports during April-December 1996 was worth $1.1 billion, up from $717.38 million in the same period last year, the statement said.
